title: Which dynasty ruled an important part of northern Tamil Nadu before the rise of the Imperial Cholas?
description: Identify the dynasty associated with Kanchipuram and major developments in South Indian temple architecture.
hint: Their capital was Kanchipuram.
summary: The Pallavas ruled a major part of northern Tamil Nadu and were centered at Kanchipuram.

title: What was the capital of the Pallavas?
description: Identify the principal political and cultural center of the Pallava kingdom.
hint: It is an important historic city in present-day Tamil Nadu.
summary: Kanchipuram was the principal capital of the Pallavas.

title: Which Pallava ruler is regarded as one of the earliest important rulers of the dynasty?
description: Identify the ruler associated with the early consolidation of Pallava power.
hint: His name appears frequently in discussions of early Pallava history.
summary: Simhavishnu was an important early Pallava ruler who expanded Pallava influence southward.

title: Who succeeded Simhavishnu as an important Pallava ruler?
description: Identify the Pallava ruler who was known for his patronage of architecture and literature.
hint: He was the father of Narasimhavarman I.
summary: Mahendravarman I succeeded Simhavishnu and became an important Pallava ruler.

title: Which Pallava ruler was known by the title Gunabhara?
description: Identify the Pallava ruler associated with this title.
hint: He was an important patron of art and literature.
summary: Mahendravarman I was known by several titles, including Gunabhara.

title: Which Pallava ruler fought the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II?
description: Identify the Pallava ruler who faced the Chalukya invasion led by Pulakeshin II.
hint: He was the father of Narasimhavarman I.
summary: Mahendravarman I fought against the Chalukya ruler Pulakeshin II.

title: Who defeated the Chalukya ruler Pulakeshin II?
description: Identify the Pallava ruler who defeated Pulakeshin II and later captured Vatapi.
hint: He was known as Vatapikonda.
summary: Narasimhavarman I defeated Pulakeshin II and captured Vatapi.

title: What title did Narasimhavarman I adopt after capturing Vatapi?
description: Identify the title associated with his victory over the Chalukyas.
hint: The title literally refers to the conqueror of Vatapi.
summary: Narasimhavarman I adopted the title Vatapikonda after capturing Vatapi.

title: Which Pallava ruler was also known as Mamalla?
description: Identify the Pallava ruler whose title gave Mahabalipuram its historical name Mamallapuram.
hint: He succeeded Mahendravarman I.
summary: Narasimhavarman I was known as Mamalla, meaning great wrestler.

title: What is the present-day name of Mamallapuram?
description: Identify the modern name of the Pallava-era port and artistic center.
hint: It is famous for its Shore Temple and rock-cut monuments.
summary: Mamallapuram is commonly known today as Mahabalipuram.

title: Which Pallava ruler built many structural temples at Kanchipuram?
description: Identify the Pallava ruler associated with the mature structural temple tradition.
hint: He was also known as Rajasimha.
summary: Narasimhavarman II, also known as Rajasimha, was a major patron of structural temples.

title: Which Pallava ruler was also called Rajasimha?
description: Identify the Pallava ruler associated with the title Rajasimha.
hint: He was famous for temple construction.
summary: Narasimhavarman II was also known as Rajasimha.

title: Which temple is an important Pallava structural temple at Kanchipuram?
description: Identify the famous temple associated with Narasimhavarman II.
hint: It is dedicated to Shiva.
summary: The Kailasanatha Temple at Kanchipuram was built under Narasimhavarman II.

title: Which deity is worshipped in the Kailasanatha Temple at Kanchipuram?
description: Identify the principal deity of this famous Pallava temple.
hint: The temple is a major Shaiva monument.
summary: The Kailasanatha Temple is dedicated to Shiva.

title: Which famous Pallava monument stands on the shore at Mahabalipuram?
description: Identify the temple that became an iconic monument of Pallava architecture.
hint: Its name reflects its location beside the sea.
summary: The Shore Temple is one of the most famous Pallava monuments at Mahabalipuram.

title: The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram is mainly associated with which dynasty?
description: Identify the dynasty responsible for this famous coastal monument.
hint: The dynasty was centered at Kanchipuram.
summary: The Shore Temple is a major monument of the Pallava dynasty.

title: Which group of monuments at Mahabalipuram is famous for monolithic rathas?
description: Identify the Pallava monuments carved from single rocks.
hint: They are named after the five Pandava brothers.
summary: The Pancha Rathas are famous monolithic rock-cut monuments at Mahabalipuram.

title: The Pancha Rathas are located at which place?
description: Identify the famous Pallava artistic center where the Pancha Rathas are located.
hint: It is also called Mamallapuram.
summary: The Pancha Rathas are located at Mahabalipuram in Tamil Nadu.

title: Which Pallava ruler is associated with the Pancha Rathas?
description: Identify the ruler under whose reign the monolithic rathas were developed.
hint: He was known by the title Mamalla.
summary: The Pancha Rathas are generally associated with the reign of Narasimhavarman I.

title: Which famous relief is found at Mahabalipuram?
description: Identify the monumental rock relief also known as Arjuna's Penance.
hint: It depicts numerous figures, including celestial beings and animals.
summary: The Descent of the Ganges, popularly called Arjuna's Penance, is a famous Mahabalipuram relief.

title: What type of architecture was pioneered prominently by the Pallavas at Mahabalipuram?
description: Identify the architectural technique represented by the early Pallava monuments.
hint: Several monuments were carved directly into natural rock.
summary: Rock-cut architecture developed prominently under the Pallavas at Mahabalipuram.

title: Which Pallava ruler is associated with the transition from rock-cut to structural temples?
description: Identify the ruler whose reign witnessed important developments in Pallava temple architecture.
hint: His successor Narasimhavarman I was known as Mamalla.
summary: Mahendravarman I is associated with early rock-cut temples, while later Pallavas developed structural temples.

title: Which Pallava ruler authored the Sanskrit work Mattavilasa Prahasana?
description: Identify the ruler who was also known for his literary abilities.
hint: He was a patron of art and literature.
summary: Mahendravarman I is traditionally credited with composing Mattavilasa Prahasana.

title: Mattavilasa Prahasana is written in which language?
description: Identify the classical language in which Mahendravarman I's play was composed.
hint: It was widely used in royal and scholarly writings in ancient India.
summary: Mattavilasa Prahasana was composed in Sanskrit.

title: Which Chinese traveler visited the Pallava kingdom during the reign of Narasimhavarman II?
description: Identify the famous Chinese Buddhist pilgrim who visited South India.
hint: He traveled to India during the 7th century.
summary: The Chinese traveler Xuanzang visited the Pallava kingdom during the 7th century.

title: Which religion received significant patronage from some Pallava rulers?
description: Identify the religious tradition strongly represented in Pallava monuments and literature.
hint: The Kailasanatha and Shore temples are dedicated to Shiva.
summary: Shaivism received significant patronage under several Pallava rulers.

title: Which Bhakti saints were associated with Shaivism in the Pallava period?
description: Identify the Tamil Shaiva devotional saints who flourished during this period.
hint: They are known as the Nayanars.
summary: The Nayanars were Tamil Shaiva Bhakti saints associated with the Pallava and later periods.

title: Which Bhakti saints were associated with Vaishnavism in the Pallava period?
description: Identify the Tamil Vaishnava devotional saints.
hint: Their hymns are collected in the Divya Prabandham.
summary: The Alvars were Tamil Vaishnava Bhakti saints.

title: Which Pallava temple is dedicated to Vishnu and located in Kanchipuram?
description: Identify the famous Vaishnava temple built during the Pallava period.
hint: Its name refers to Vishnu as Vaikuntha.
summary: The Vaikuntha Perumal Temple at Kanchipuram is an important Pallava temple dedicated to Vishnu.

title: Which architectural style is most closely associated with the Pallava temples?
description: Identify the broad South Indian architectural tradition represented by Pallava temples.
hint: It is the major temple style of southern India.
summary: Pallava temples are important early examples of the Dravidian architectural tradition.

title: Which script developed significantly in South India under Pallava influence?
description: Identify the script that became influential in Southeast Asia through South Indian cultural contacts.
hint: It influenced several Southeast Asian scripts.
summary: The Pallava script influenced the development of several scripts in Southeast Asia.

title: Pallava script had a major cultural influence on which region?
description: Identify the region where scripts derived from or influenced by Pallava writing became important.
hint: Think of maritime Southeast Asia.
summary: Pallava script influenced writing systems in Southeast Asia.

title: Which dynasty was a major rival of the Pallavas in the Deccan?
description: Identify the dynasty whose rulers repeatedly fought the Pallavas.
hint: Pulakeshin II belonged to this dynasty.
summary: The Chalukyas of Badami were major rivals of the Pallavas.

title: What was the capital of the Chalukyas who fought the Pallavas?
description: Identify the capital of the Chalukyas of Badami.
hint: It is a historic town in present-day Karnataka.
summary: Badami, ancient Vatapi, was the capital of the Chalukyas who fought the Pallavas.

title: What was the ancient name of Badami?
description: Identify the ancient name of the Chalukya capital captured by Narasimhavarman I.
hint: Narasimhavarman I adopted a title connected with its conquest.
summary: Badami was known in ancient times as Vatapi.

title: Which famous Chinese traveler described Kanchipuram?
description: Identify the Chinese Buddhist pilgrim whose account provides information about South India.
hint: He visited India in the 7th century.
summary: Xuanzang visited Kanchipuram and described the Pallava kingdom.

title: Which Pallava monument is an example of a monolithic temple?
description: Identify one of the famous temples carved from a single mass of rock.
hint: It is one of the Pancha Rathas.
summary: The Dharmaraja Ratha is one of the monolithic Pancha Rathas at Mahabalipuram.

title: Which animal motif is especially prominent in Pallava architecture?
description: Identify an animal motif frequently represented in Pallava monuments.
hint: It is associated with strength and royal symbolism.
summary: The lion is a prominent motif in Pallava art and architecture.

title: Which temple is one of the earliest examples of a free-standing structural stone temple in South India?
description: Identify the Pallava temple associated with the early development of structural temple architecture.
hint: It is located in Kanchipuram.
summary: The Kailasanatha Temple at Kanchipuram is an important early structural stone temple.

title: Which Pallava ruler is associated with the construction of the Shore Temple?
description: Identify the ruler whose reign is generally associated with the Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram.
hint: He was also known as Rajasimha.
summary: The Shore Temple is generally associated with Narasimhavarman II, also known as Rajasimha.

title: Which Pallava ruler was a contemporary of the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II?
description: Identify the Pallava ruler who faced the Chalukya invasion.
hint: He was succeeded by Narasimhavarman I.
summary: Mahendravarman I was a contemporary and rival of Pulakeshin II.

title: Who was the famous general of Narasimhavarman I who captured Vatapi?
description: Identify the Pallava military commander associated with the defeat of the Chalukyas.
hint: He is also known as Paranjothi.
summary: Paranjothi, also known as Siruthondar, was a famous general under Narasimhavarman I.

title: Which Pallava ruler was known for his interest in Jainism before supporting Shaivism?
description: Identify the ruler traditionally associated with a religious transformation.
hint: He was the father of Narasimhavarman I.
summary: Mahendravarman I is traditionally described as having moved from Jainism toward Shaivism.

title: Which saint is traditionally associated with the conversion of Mahendravarman I to Shaivism?
description: Identify the famous Shaiva saint connected with this traditional account.
hint: He was one of the major Nayanar saints.
summary: Appar, also known as Tirunavukkarasar, is traditionally associated with Mahendravarman I's conversion to Shaivism.

title: Which Pallava ruler founded or developed the city of Mamallapuram as a major artistic center?
description: Identify the ruler whose title gave the city its name.
hint: His title was Mamalla.
summary: Narasimhavarman I, known as Mamalla, played a major role in developing Mamallapuram.

title: Which Pallava temple is associated with Vaishnavism?
description: Identify the temple dedicated to Vishnu at Kanchipuram.
hint: The temple's name refers to Vishnu's heavenly abode.
summary: The Vaikuntha Perumal Temple is an important Pallava Vaishnava temple.

title: Which Pallava ruler was associated with the later phase of the dynasty and the famous Vaikuntha Perumal Temple?
description: Identify the ruler associated with the construction of the Vaikuntha Perumal Temple.
hint: He belonged to the Nandivarman line.
summary: Nandivarman II Pallavamalla is traditionally associated with the Vaikuntha Perumal Temple.

title: Which dynasty eventually replaced Pallava political dominance in much of Tamil Nadu?
description: Identify the dynasty that rose to prominence after the decline of Pallava power.
hint: Its early imperial ruler was Vijayalaya.
summary: The Cholas eventually replaced the Pallavas as the dominant power in much of Tamil Nadu.

title: The monuments at Mahabalipuram are recognized by UNESCO under which category?
description: Identify the UNESCO designation associated with the Pallava monuments.
hint: They are recognized for their outstanding cultural value.
summary: The Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: What is the major historical significance of the Pallavas?
description: Identify the contribution for which the Pallavas are especially remembered in South Indian history.
hint: Think of temples, sculpture and the development of South Indian architecture.
summary: The Pallavas played a major role in the development of South Indian temple architecture, sculpture and the spread of cultural influences.

options.title: Development of South Indian temple architecture
